styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, markets and the colonial heart of the city.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Cathedral, Plaza Libertad and the memory sites.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Volcano views and green escapes above the valley.

stays.why: Hotels, restaurants and bars within walking distance; a good base for first-timers.
Quieter, greener streets with malls and cafés; short taxi rides to the centre.
Upscale and walkable, next to Zona Rosa and the museums; calm at night.
Cheapest and closest to the cathedral and plazas; busier and less polished at night.

food: Try pupusas, the national dish: thick corn tortillas stuffed with cheese, beans or pork, usually USD 1–2 each.
Eat at a pupusería for lunch or dinner; revueltas (mixed) and queso con loroco are safe first choices.
Breakfast: fried plantains, beans and cream, or a tamal wrapped in banana leaf.
Zona Rosa and Escalón have the widest choice of restaurants, from local to international.
Street food is cheap and tasty; pick busy stalls and drink bottled water.
more_time: Add a day trip to the Joya de Cerén ruins, a UNESCO site often called the Pompeii of the Americas; check opening days before you go.
Swap an afternoon for the Museo de Arte de El Salvador (MARTE) in San Benito.
Climb to a viewpoint above the city, such as the Devil's Door area, with a guide and in daylight.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the historic centre, the museums and a good food day; add a third for a day trip outside the city.

month_notes: Dry and warm: highs near 30°C, lows around 19°C, only about 2 rain days. Great for walking.
The driest month, about 1 rain day. Sunny days, cool-ish evenings.
Warm and mostly dry, but rain days jump to about 6. Carry a light rain jacket.
The rainy season starts: about 16 rain days. Plan indoor sights and go out in the mornings.
Wet: about 26 rain days and slightly cooler highs near 29°C. Expect afternoon downpours.
The wettest stretch: about 27 rain days, highs near 27°C. Pack a raincoat and waterproof shoes.
Still wet, about 24 rain days. Mornings are usually the best window.
Wet again, about 26 rain days. Keep plans flexible.
The wettest month, about 29 rain days. Indoor museums and cafés are the safe bet.
Still very wet, about 26 rain days. Check road conditions for any day trip.
Rain eases to about 14 rain days. A good shoulder month.
Dry and pleasant: about 4 rain days, highs near 29°C. A strong month to visit.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical highland climate: warm all year, with a sharp dry season from November to March and a long, wet season from May to October.

items.title: Best time: November to March
items.text: Highs around 29–31°C, lows near 19°C, and few rain days. Ideal for walking the centre.

items.title: Wet season: May to October
items.text: Rain on 24–29 days a month. Showers often hit in the afternoon; do outdoor sights early.

items.title: Warm year-round
items.text: Highs stay between 27 and 31°C every month. Evenings are mild, around 19–21°C.

items.title: Pack rain gear in the wet months
items.text: A light raincoat or umbrella and quick-dry shoes help from May to October.

items.title: Cooler, greener hills
items.text: The wet months turn the hills around the city lush; views are best on clear mornings.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes, sunscreen and a hat; a light layer for evenings; rain protection if you visit May to October.

transit.best: Uber, InDrive or a taxi with the fare agreed first; walk only in Zona Rosa and San Benito.

modes.text: No metro or tram. The city relies on buses.
City buses are cheap but crowded. Keep valuables close.
Taxis are common; agree the fare before you get in. Uber and InDrive work in the city and to the airport.
Driving is possible, but traffic and aggressive driving make it stressful.
Walking suits Zona Rosa and San Benito; other areas are spread out.
